messages:
arjun: Heads-up — trying to onboard llama-3-small-q4 into the eval harness and hit a weird tokenizer/padding interaction that breaks our chat templates. Anyone seen padding bytes leak into prompts?

maria: can you paste an example input/output? quick guess: pad token id mismatch?

arjun: sample sequence (trimmed):
```
input_ids: [101, 345, 998, 2, 0, 0, 0]  # model q4 export seems to use 0 for pad
decoded: 'Assistant: Hello\x00\x00\x00'
```
behavior: chat template expects to strip trailing pads but after tokenization we get \"\x00\" characters in middle of assistant turn sometimes when user message ends with punctuation.

devon: ugh, that smells like tokenizer config mismatch between the saved tokenizer.json and the quantized model's vocab mapping. Did the export script reassign pad to id 0?

arjun: I traced the model checkpoint — export used `pad_token_id=0` while our eval config assumes `pad_token_id=1`. Changing the eval config to match fixes most cases but fails for the chat runner when prompts include trailing spaces.

sophia: Relatedly, the eval-runner crashed on the quantized model with `RuntimeError: dynamic shape not supported for KV cache` yesterday — might be the cause for CI flakiness. logs attached in the PR.

arjun: repro steps I used:
```bash
# local runner
python run_eval.py --model ./llama3-q4 --prompt-template chat_v2 --batch-size 1
# got weird decoded strings and sometimes runner OOM + dynamic shape error
```

maria: quick mitigation: update chat_v2 template to explicitly strip pad tokens before concatenating turns, and add `tokenizer.pad_token = '<|pad|>'` mapping in the model config. Could do a patch in infra until the export is fixed.

sophia: agree. I can open a small PR that normalizes `pad_token_id` from the model meta when onboarding and emits a warning if it differs from tokenizer.json. That should reduce surprises in CI.

devon: also we need a unit test in the eval-harness that runs the tokenization roundtrip for short chat templates — currently our CI matrix skips tiny-models with q4. Add `tests/tokenization_roundtrip/test_chat_templates.py` and run it on the new model.

arjun: +1. Also noticed our dashboard (eval-run-dashboard) wasn't picking up the run id for the quantized rollout — looks like the runner didn't attach `model_revision` tag when the model path contains hyphens. Small parsing bug.

maria: filed an issue for dashboard ingestion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-run-dashboard/issues/412 — minimal fix is to relax tag parsing regex.

sophia: CI noise: `ci-bot` posted a flaky failure on `eval-smoke-quant` yesterday at 03:12 UTC. It retried and passed. We should make the smoke test retryable and add a more diagnostic dump on the first failure (tokenizer config + model meta).

ci-bot: [ci] job eval-smoke-quant failed on runner-03 (attempt 1) — requeued (attempt 2). Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/22345/logs

arjun: thanks. Plan: (1) patch eval harness to normalize pad_token_id and strip pads in chat templates (PR arjun/llama3-pad-fix), (2) add tokenization roundtrip unit, (3) add runner diagnostic dump on smoke failures, (4) dashboard tag parsing patch. I'll kick off the PRs today and tag people.

maria: ping me for review on the tokenizer changes — will also run local evals against the quantized artifact.

devon: I'll take the unit test + CI retry work.

sophia: I'll do the dashboard patch and the ingestion regression test.

arjun: awesome, thanks. leaving a note: if anyone is onboarding other q4 models, please double-check `pad_token_id` and run this snippet before full eval: `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json'); print(t.get_vocab().get('<|pad|>'))"`

maria: saved — should reduce future surprises. :thumbsup:
